item.excerpt:encoded:
On one wall in the pub is an illustration by Xena Jonasson, who also works there, calls for yaghuudaang — respect — in the pub.
"I really like having that sign," says Lunner. "You can just point at it if somebody's acting out of line."

item.title: Web_Haida Nation Recognition Act signing @ George Brown_20240414_0294
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: From left to right, B.C. Premier David Eby, Council of the Haida Nation president Jason Alsop, Gaagwiis, and B.C. Minister of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation Murray Rankin sign the Haida Title Lands Agreement in Skidegate on April 14. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: Riley-Dorman
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: Student Riley Dorman sits with his dog, Lola, by Lon Sharp's salmon sculpture, "The Spirit of Sandspit." (Submitted photo)

item.title: Web_MassetGroundbreakings_053024_1150
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: Masset Mayor Sheri Disney, with yellow shovel, breaks ground on a new pedestrian boardwalk project at the Main Street pier in Masset on May 31 together with Tenille Thompson, a landscape architect with Urban Systems. From left to right are Terry Carty and Barry Pages, village councillors; Andrew Baigent, Urban Systems' community planning lead; Tenille Thompson; Bret Johnston, village councillor; Sheri Disney; Joshua Humphries, chief administrative officer for the Village of Masset; and Joe Geluch, president of Naikoon Contracting. (Andrew Hudson photo/Haida Gwaii News)

item.title: Web_WorldOceanDay@KayCentre_20240608_0434
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: Gwaii Haanas interpreter Meighan Wilson, Ḵuuyas Jaad, welcomes a gumboot-ed crowd to a low-tide walk at Second Beach in Skidegate on June 8, World Ocean Day. (Andrew Hudson photo/Haida Gwaii News)

item.title: Web_Auroras @ North Beach_20240511_0353
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: Aurora borealis shimmer purple and white, lighting up a lost, deerbone-decorated Croc shoe on North Beach on Saturday, May 11 after an extraordinarily powerful solar flare. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: Web_East Beach Medevac_05182024_1
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: BC paramedics load an injured man onto a waiting helicopter along East Beach on Saturday, May 18. Volunteers with Old Massett Volunteer Fire Department and Archipelago Ground Search and Rescue drove around Rose Spit and down the beach to help stretcher-carry the man to the helicopter and provide patient care. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: Web_TamaraDavidsonNorthCoastNDPCandidate_060824_1483
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: BC NDP candidate Tamara Davidson, Laanas, has been elected to represent North Coast-Haida Gwaii in the B.C. legislature. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: Web_HiellenUnveilling_062124_1991
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: At centre, Ed Davis, Iihlangaa K’adangaa, leads students from Tahayghen Elementary in singing the Happy Song after the unveilling of the new welcome sign for the Hiellen Village Longhouses on June 21. Behind, Haida carver Lyle Campbell, T'aaw Tlaahl, gets a congratulatory hug for his work. (Andrew Hudson/Haida Gwaii News)

item.title: Web_Sphenia-Jones-potluck-@-Sarah's-Longhouse_20240517_0012
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: Haida elder Sphenia Jones spoke at a May 17 dinner at Sarah’s Longhouse in Old Massett. The dinner was held for Jones other Haida residential school survivors to connect and share their stories. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: Web_MassetDanceTroupe_062224_2817
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: The Masset Dance Troupe’s end-of-season highlighted all they learned in a season with several mentors and shows on- and off-island. A half-day summer camp is planned for August 6 to 10, with a pop-up show at the Edge of the World Music Festival. (Andrew Hudson photos)

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_2936 copy
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “It’s only because of the strength of the Indigenous leadership across this country, this province, and the Haida WNation, for pushing the courts, pushing on the ground, doing the right thing, that the situation has changed.” — CHN President Gaagwiis, Jason Alsop

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3092
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: Gaagwiis, Jason Alsop, holds a copper while singers and drummers Donnie Edenshaw, left, and Guujaaw, right, perform the Haida national anthem on July 5. (Andrew Hudson photos)

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3341
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “This country needs Indigenous people back at the helm. Without us, look at where we’re at. We talk about global warming, because the Indigenous voice has been silenced too long.” — Chief Joe Alphonse

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3377
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “You gave us hope. You gave Canada hope about what it could be to govern your land within your law, to govern your land as your ancestors did since time out of mind.” — Sundance Chief Reuben George, Tsleil-Waututh

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3476
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “I thank our nation. I thank our people for fighting. I thank our people for persevering.” — Gya awhlans, Roy Collison

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3488
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: Emcee Desi Collison congratulates a boy who danced for everyone to get a lost necklace back. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3547
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “Now, the future will be what we make of it, not what somebody else dishes out to us… Ideally, we come to eco-topia where everything’s good and all the trees are growing. Everybody’s getting along.” — Gidansda, Guujaaw

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3558
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “All our ancestors were so active in fishing... I look forward to the next few years, because they will determine whether we can negotiate a return of those resources in the ocean or whether it’s something decided in court.” — Nang Jingwas, Russ Jones

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3574
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “We were the stewards of these lands and these waters. It’s taken us a long time to get to this level. Now, we need to step it up. It’s all these young people that we see in the hall today that are going to be our future leaders.” — Gyahgujaang, Robert Russ

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3585
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “We can’t fight B.C. anymore, because they gave us Haida Gwaii back. So the biggest fight we’ve got now is amongst ourselves, as Haidas.” — Wiigaanad, Sidney G. Crosby

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3698
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: The Hltaaxuulang Gud ad K’aaju, Friends Together Singing, perform at the celebration feast. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3714
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: The Hltaaxuulang Gud ad K’aaju, Friends Together Singing, perform at the celebration feast. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3721
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: The Hltaaxuulang Gud ad K’aaju, Friends Together Singing, perform at the celebration feast. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3751
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: The Hltaaxuulang Gud ad K’aaju, Friends Together Singing, perform at the celebration feast. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3814
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: The Hltaaxuulang Gud ad K’aaju, Friends Together Singing, perform at the celebration feast. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3889
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “We will resolve Haida title to Haida Gwaii. We’re not passing this on to our next generation. And that means not only to the land, but to the ocean and to the freshwaters.” — Terri-Lynn Williams-Davidson

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3890
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “We’re in exactly the same place as we should have been, right at the very beginning when the Crown asserted sovereignty and should have recognized Haida title, inherent title to all of Haida Gwaii.” — Louise Mandell, Q.C.

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3904
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “Now it’s up to us to build a house together, to form community, to show respect and love for each other, and to create a better, more prosperous future for everyone on Haida Gwaii.” — Murray Rankin, Minister of Indigenous Relations

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3935
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “We’re not giving you anything back. It’s always been yours. We’re just finally owning up to the truth.” — Jennifer Rice, North Coast MLA

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_3945
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “We have difficult issues to sort out. We know that if we sit down and negotiate in good faith and respect, that we will be able to achieve an outcome that holds all of us up, that makes us all greater.” — Doug White, special counsel to the Premier

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_4007
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “As someone who lives up the Skeena River and is raising two daughters with my partner in this beautiful part of the world, I believe, fundamentally, that if we do right by the first peoples of this place, we are all better off.” — Taylor Bachrach, Skeena—Bulkley Valley MP

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_4020
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: The Tluu Xaadaa Naay dance group performs at the close of the celebration feast. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: HaidaTitleFeast_070524_4032
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: “We’re all stronger together, even when some of our people sit on the other side of the table. We ask questions. We ask tough questions. That makes us stronger. — Kihlguulans, Christian White

item.title: HannaEdenshaw_EnergyForum_092124_6170
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: Above, Hanna Edenshaw gives the keynote speech at the Swiilawiid symposium on Sept. 21. Edenshaw is one of 15 youth suing the Canadian government not for money, but for a science-based climate plan. “What happens to Haida Gwaii in the climate crisis isn’t only affected by what we do,” she said. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: Gaagwiis_EnergyForum_092124_6162
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: Gaagwiis, Jason Alsop, President of the Council of the Haida Nation, opens the symposium on Saturday, Sept. 21 by speaking about the large-scale work needed to get Haida Gwaii off diesel power, and things people can do at the personal level to live more sustainably. "At times, for a lot of people, I know it can be a heavy thing to think about what we're confronted with here — systems change in a system where everything has been built around cheap fossil fuels," he said. "We're seeing that system come to a place where it isn't working." (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: EzraBeaton_EnergyForum_092224_6139
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: Musician Ezra Beaton sings an original song about the impact of climate change, seen over the shoulder of his father, Jacob Beaton, founder of Tea Creek Farm. Tea Creek has trained hundreds of people in Indigenous agriculture and food sovereignty on a farm that produces tens of thousands of pounds of fresh produce. (Andrew Hudson photo)

item.title: GKNS-Breakers-at-provincial-final-in-Kamloops
item.dc:creator: stacey
item.excerpt:encoded: The Gidgalang Kuuyas Naay Secondary girls soccer team played in a 16-team provincial Zones tournament in Kamloops last week. "We had five games, we fought hard," said Steve Querenjung, who coached the team along with Katrina Husband. "We managed to really learn a lot as a team and start to work through the nerves and find ourselves." Five players won Player of the Game awards, including Mya Williams, a Grade 9 goalkeeper named as one of the top 16 players in the tournament, as well as Camryn Greenough, Allison Beachy, Alaa Sirhan, and Claire Swain. Travel funding for the team was provided by Gwaii Trust, School District 50, and parent volunteers. At a banquet before the tournament, the Breakers shared the Haida women's dance, using a recording by Donnie Edenshaw of Old Massett. Nearly every girl in the hall, more than 300, joined in. (Submitted photo)

item.title: BrentButtinDG
item.dc:creator: andrewhudson
item.excerpt:encoded: Comedian Brent Butt does stand-up at the Daajing Giids Community Hall on Oct. 6. “We’ve got Skidegate here," he said. "Sounds like something you’d say when you’re running from the cops: 'Let’s Skidaget out of here.'” When he asked the crowd what Skidegate means, a Haida citizen gave him a deep explanation that left Butt blankly staring at the crowd before laughing and saying he “got more than he was ready to digest.” (Rhonda Lee Russ photo)
